title_en: Xie Minshi v. Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company — dispute over equity interests
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over equity transfer; First instance; Intermediate People's Court; Shanghai Municipality; Natural person; Legal person; Law on Sino-Foreign Cooperative Joint Ventures; Contract Law; Validity of equity transfer agreement; Legal effect of board resolution; Obligation to register equity change; Equity transfer; Board resolution; Sino-foreign cooperative enterprise; Equity dispute of Jingang Company
full_text_en:
Xie Minshi v. Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company — Dispute over Equity Transfer

Plaintiff: Xie Minshi, male, 52 years old, a citizen of the United States of America. Domicile: California, United States of America.

Defendant: Zhang Ruichang, male, 53 years old, a citizen of the United States of America. Domicile: California, United States of America.

Defendant: Shanghai Jingang Casting Co., Ltd. Domicile: Jiading District, Shanghai, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Zhang Ruichang, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

The plaintiff, Xie Minshi, filed an action with the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court against the defendants Zhang Ruichang and Shanghai Jingang Casting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jingang Company) regarding a dispute over equity transfer.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff and the defendant Zhang Ruichang were former college classmates. Zhang Ruichang proposed transferring 20% of his shares in the defendant Jingang Company to the plaintiff. Relying on trust in his old classmate, the plaintiff, at the price proposed by Zhang Ruichang, remitted a total of USD 400,000 to Jingang Company. He was listed as the vice-chairman of the board of directors of Jingang Company as an investor but never participated in the management of Jingang Company. In September 1999, when the plaintiff was invited to temporarily manage the company, he discovered that Zhang Ruichang had not, as agreed in the contract and articles of association, injected into Jingang Company the USD 2.11 million in cash and production equipment worth USD 890,000 that he had promised to contribute. Instead, Zhang Ruichang had used the funds invested by the plaintiff as his own capital contribution for capital verification, and during the management period, he had also engaged in irregular operations and infringed upon the rights and interests of other shareholders. For this reason, the plaintiff demanded to withdraw from Jingang Company and that Zhang Ruichang repurchase at the original price the 20% equity that Zhang Ruichang had transferred to him. Zhang Ruichang agreed and reached an agreement with the plaintiff. They drafted the "Equity Transfer Agreement," but when the signing was imminent, Zhang Ruichang changed the payment terms, causing the signing to fail. The parties then decided to replace the equity transfer contract with a resolution of the Jingang Company board of directors. On March 13, 2000, the board of directors of Jingang Company adopted two resolutions, A and B (hereinafter referred to as the "March 13 Resolutions"), agreeing that the plaintiff would transfer his 20% equity in Jingang Company to Zhang Ruichang for USD 400,000; agreeing that within two days after the signing of the resolutions, the property at Room 404, Building 7, Lane 65, Jinshajiang Road, purchased by the company, would be transferred to the plaintiff at a price of RMB 421,145, and at the same time, RMB 1.5 million from the sale proceeds of the ground-floor shop at No. 69, Jinshajiang Road would be paid to the plaintiff first, with the remaining balance to be paid by Jingang Company to the plaintiff by issuing a time bank draft each month; if any installment was overdrawn or returned unpaid, the plaintiff would have the right to claim all unmatured claims. Since Zhang Ruichang was in fact the sole investor of Jingang Company, Zhang Ruichang's payment to the plaintiff was equivalent to Jingang Company's payment to the plaintiff. After the board resolutions were made, the plaintiff left Jingang Company, and Zhang Ruichang had already announced to the employees the news of the plaintiff's withdrawal of equity. However, Zhang Ruichang did not transfer the property at Room 404, Building 7, Lane 65, Jinshajiang Road to the plaintiff, and Jingang Company did not issue a time bank draft to the plaintiff to pay the remaining balance. The plaintiff believes that although the equity transfer agreement had not been registered with the relevant government authorities, it was a contract lawfully formed and had legal binding force. Now, Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company have failed to pay the corresponding equity transfer price to the plaintiff according to the agreement, constituting a breach of contract. To protect his own lawful rights and interests, the plaintiff therefore files this action, requesting a judgment ordering Zhang Ruichang to immediately pay the plaintiff the equity transfer price of USD 400,000, or RMB 3,311,600 converted at the exchange rate of 1:8.279; and ordering Jingang Company to bear joint and several liability for this debt of Zhang Ruichang.

The plaintiff, Xie Minshi, submitted the following evidence:

1. The industrial and commercial registration materials of Jingang Company to prove the status of the original shareholders of Jingang Company;
2. The remittance vouchers for Xie Minshi's payment of investment funds and the approval certificate and business license after the change of shareholders to prove Xie Minshi's investment situation. These pieces of evidence also prove that as of June 2000, the actual paid-in registered capital of Jingang Company was USD 500,000.
3. A letter of inquiry sent by Xie Minshi to Zhang Ruichang on October 17, 1999, to prove the reason for Xie Minshi's withdrawal of equity.
4. A reply letter from Zhang Ruichang to Xie Minshi on October 22, 1999.
5. The draft of the "Equity Transfer Agreement" and the fax correspondence between Xie Minshi and Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company regarding the equity transfer matter, to prove that there was a full consultation process for the equity withdrawal.
6. Board Resolutions A and B of Jingang Company made on March 13, 2000, stipulating that Xie Minshi would transfer his 20% shares in Jingang Company to Zhang Ruichang at a price of USD 400,000.

Defendant Zhang Ruichang's Defense: The defendant Jingang Company is a Sino-foreign cooperative enterprise established by me and a non-party entity, Shanghai Lixin Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lixin Company). To become a shareholder, the plaintiff Xie Minshi remitted a total of USD 392,908.64 to Jingang Company, not USD 400,000. Xie Minshi's funds were remitted to Jingang Company, and Jingang Company is not my private enterprise. There is no factual basis for Xie Minshi listing me as a defendant in this case. It is true that on March 13, 2000, the board of directors of Jingang Company made a resolution, with all directors agreeing that I would purchase Xie Minshi's 20% equity. According to the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Cooperative Enterprises, a change in the equity of a company cannot be accomplished by a board resolution alone; it must be approved by the examination and approval authority and registered by the registration authority. This board resolution also resolved to offset the equity transfer price against two properties of Jingang Company, which would be transferred to Xie Minshi. If this were implemented, it would result in a reduction of the registered capital of the cooperative company, which is contrary to legal provisions. Although the board resolved to transfer Xie Minshi's equity worth more than RMB 3 million to me, using the form of a board resolution does not meet legal requirements. According to the Economic Contract Law, economic contracts must be in writing, except for those settled immediately. After the resolution, Xie Minshi did not enter into a written contract for the transfer with me. Based on the above reasons, Xie Minshi's current claim for payment of the equity transfer price based on the March 13, 2000 board resolution of Jingang Company is illegal, and his claims should not be supported.

Evidence submitted by defendant Zhang Ruichang:

1. The credit vouchers for Jingang Company's receipt of Xie Minshi's investment, which record that Xie Minshi's total investment amounted to USD 392,908.64.

Defendant Jingang Company's Defense: This case is a dispute over equity between shareholders and has no relation to this Company.

During the trial, the plaintiff Xie Minshi added an additional claim on the grounds that the defendants Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company wilfully failed to go through the equity change procedures with the government authorities, artificially creating obstacles for litigation: an order that Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company go through all legal procedures with the relevant government authorities arising from the change of shareholders and equity.

The plaintiff Xie Minshi also additionally submitted the following evidence:

7. A fax sent by Zhang Ruichang to his daughter, informing her of the fact that Xie Minshi had transferred his shares.
8. Letters sent by Xie Minshi on November 18, 2000 and December 18, 2000, urging Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company to go through the equity transfer procedures.
9. A letter from Xie Minshi to Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company on January 18, 2001, requesting Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company not to transfer the shop property at No. 69, Jinshajiang Road or other assets.
10. A certificate issued on July 21, 2000 by the office of the Jiading District Foreign Economic Relations and Trade Commission of Shanghai, stating that since March 13, 2000, Jingang Company had not applied to it for a change of items in the original approval certificate.

In response to the additional claim of the plaintiff Xie Minshi, the defendants Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company argued: Because the sale of the ground-floor house at No. 69, Jinshajiang Road could not be completed as agreed, and because Xie Minshi had requested the relevant government departments to suspend the equity change procedures of Jingang Company, Jingang Company was unable to complete the equity change procedures, not that it was deliberately delaying. On December 5, 2000, at a meeting that Xie Minshi, under an excuse, refused to attend, Jingang Company held a board meeting and adopted a resolution "Resolving to Terminate the Implementation of Resolutions A and B of March 13, 2000" (hereinafter referred to as the "December 5 Resolution"). Therefore, the factual premise for Xie Minshi's withdrawal of equity no longer exists, and his claim for payment of the equity transfer price cannot be sustained. Jingang Company will no longer go through the equity change procedures because of Xie Minshi, and Xie Minshi's additional claim should also not be supported. Moreover, Xie Minshi's additional claim and his original claim involve two different legal relationships and should be filed and tried separately.

The defendants Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company additionally submitted the following evidence:

2. A letter dated May 12, 2000 from lawyers Zhu Zengjin and Yang Congxing of Jiangsu Tongren Law Firm to the "Shanghai Jiading District Foreign Economic Relations and Trade Office", stating that the case of Xie Minshi v. Zhang Ruichang concerning the cooperative enterprise dispute involving Jingang Company had been accepted by the Shanghai Sub-Commission of the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission. The two lawyers, authorized by Xie Minshi, requested the "Shanghai Jiading District Foreign Economic Relations and Trade Office" not to handle any capital increase or decrease or any other change of company matters by Zhang Ruichang according to law, pending the outcome of the case.
3. The board resolution of Jingang Company dated December 5, 2000, resolving to terminate the implementation of the "March 13 Resolutions".
4. The capital verification report dated October 23, 2000 of Shanghai Jiarui Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. This report confirms that as of April 1, 2000, Jingang Company had received capital contributions from shareholders of USD 861,398.64.

After trial, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, having comprehensively evaluated the evidence submitted by both parties, confirmed the facts of this case as follows:

In April 1997, the defendant Zhang Ruichang and a non-party entity, Lixin Company, signed the "Contract for Sino-American Cooperative Operation of Shanghai Jingang Casting Co., Ltd.", agreeing to cooperatively establish the defendant Jingang Company, with the parties to the cooperation to provide the cooperation conditions within three years from the date of issuance of the business license. On May 29 of the same year, Jingang Company was approved by the Shanghai Municipal People's Government and obtained its business license on June 10. After July 1997, the plaintiff Xie Minshi made investments and became a shareholder of Jingang Company. Later, due to disagreements between the parties concerning the funds and operations of Jingang Company, Xie Minshi requested to withdraw his equity. At the board meeting of Jingang Company attended by Xie Minshi, Zhang Ruichang, and the non-party entity Lixin Company, the "March 13 Resolutions" were adopted, agreeing that Zhang Ruichang would purchase Xie Minshi's 20% equity.

Regarding the capital of the defendant Jingang Company. The plaintiff Xie Minshi, based on the registration in the business license, believed it was only USD 500,000; the defendant Zhang Ruichang, though not disputing the registration in the business license, argued based on his own evidence No. 4 that as of April 1, 2000, the capital of Jingang Company was USD 861,398.64. Capital is the property foundation of a legal person's capacity and also a basis for society to recognize a legal person's capacity, and should be publicly disclosed. For the determination of an enterprise legal person's capital, only the valid registration on the business license can be relied upon. Until the industrial and commercial administrative authority has made a change registration for the registered capital of the enterprise legal person, it should be determined that the paid-in registered capital of Jingang Company is USD 500,000.

Regarding the amount of the plaintiff Xie Minshi's investment in the defendant Jingang Company. The defendant Zhang Ruichang, based on the credit vouchers, argued that it was USD 392,908.64; Xie Minshi initially claimed that his investment was USD 400,000 at the time of filing the action, but during the trial, considering that the bank might have deducted handling fees so that the actual investment amount might be less, he no longer disputed Zhang Ruichang's assertion. The "March 13 Resolutions" stipulated that Xie Minshi would transfer his 20% equity in Jingang Company to Zhang Ruichang at the price of USD 400,000, not that Jingang Company would refund Xie Minshi's investment. Therefore, determining the original amount of Xie Minshi's investment in Jingang Company does not have a direct relationship with the handling of this case. However, as the parties disputed this, it should be confirmed that Xie Minshi's investment in Jingang Company was USD 392,908.64.

Regarding the "December 5 Resolution". The plaintiff Xie Minshi did not dispute the authenticity of the "December 5 Resolution" itself but disputed its legality. Therefore, it should be confirmed as a matter of fact that the "December 5 Resolution" exists.

Regarding whether the defendants Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company applied to the government examination and approval authority for the equity change. The plaintiff Xie Minshi, based on his evidence No. 10, argued that Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company had never applied to the government examination and approval authority; Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company, based on their evidence No. 3, argued that they had applied, but because the lawyers authorized by Xie Minshi sent a letter to the government examination and approval authority to obstruct, the procedures were not completed. Whether an application was made and whether it was completed after application are two different legal facts. While Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company's evidence No. 3 can prove that the lawyers authorized by Xie Minshi once sent a letter requesting a halt to the procedures, it cannot prove that Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company actually applied. Apart from this, Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company did not submit any materials for applying for an equity change to the government examination and approval authority. Evidence No. 11 submitted by Xie Minshi can prove that Jingang Company did not apply to the government examination and approval authority for equity change procedures, and this should be confirmed as a fact of this case.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held:

Article 126, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Contracts for Sino-foreign equity joint ventures, Sino-foreign cooperative joint ventures, and Sino-foreign cooperative exploration and development of natural resources that are performed within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall be governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China." This case involves a dispute over an equity transfer arising from the performance of a Sino-foreign cooperative contract. According to this provision, the laws of the People's Republic of China shall apply to the trial of this case.

For the purpose of the plaintiff Xie Minshi's withdrawal from the cooperative operation of the defendant Jingang Company, he reached the "March 13 Resolutions" with the defendant Zhang Ruichang and the non-party entity Lixin Company. These resolutions not only stipulated the plan for the transfer of equity among shareholders of Jingang Company but also set forth the method by which the transferee would pay the transfer price to the transferor. The "March 13 Resolutions" have the dual character of a board resolution and an equity transfer contract. When Xie Minshi and Zhang Ruichang signed the "March 13 Resolutions", their equity transfer contract was formed. Merely in terms of the validity of the contract, this equity transfer contract is the true intention of both parties, and as this intention complies with the law, it should be recognized as having legal force. Although Zhang Ruichang later reached the "December 5 Resolution" with Lixin Company, intending to use this resolution to nullify the equity transfer contract in the "March 13 Resolutions", since the other party to the equity transfer contract, Xie Minshi, did not participate in the making of the "December 5 Resolution", the "December 5 Resolution" cannot affect the validity of the equity transfer contract.

Article 10 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Cooperative Enterprises provides: "If one party to a Sino-foreign cooperative enterprise transfers all or part of its rights and obligations under the cooperative enterprise contract, it must obtain the consent of the other party and report to the examination and approval authority for approval." Although the plaintiff Xie Minshi and the defendant Zhang Ruichang reached an equity transfer contract, and this equity transfer had obtained the consent of the board of directors of the defendant Jingang Company, according to law, it must also be reported to the examination and approval authority for approval. Because Jingang Company did not apply for equity change procedures in accordance with the "March 13 Resolutions", the equity has not been transferred to date, and the equity transfer contract has not produced the legal effect intended by the parties.

Article 139 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If, in the course of trying a case, a court finds that part of the facts have already been clearly established, it may enter judgment on that part first." The original claim of the plaintiff Xie Minshi was for an order that the defendant Zhang Ruichang pay the equity transfer price. Payment of the equity transfer price is predicated upon the approval of the equity transfer by the examination and approval authority. Given that the facts concerning the formation of the equity transfer contract between Xie Minshi and Zhang Ruichang have been established, and Xie Minshi has also made an additional claim for an order that Zhang Ruichang and the defendant Jingang Company go through the equity transfer procedures, a preliminary judgment may be rendered on Xie Minshi's additional claim in accordance with law. As for Xie Minshi's claim for payment of the equity transfer price, it shall be dealt with after the preliminary judgment takes effect, depending on the result of the examination and approval by the examination and approval authority. Accordingly, on October 24, 2001, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court ruled:

The defendants Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company shall, within 10 days from the date this judgment takes effect, go through the relevant equity change procedures with the examination and approval authority concerning the equity transfer between the plaintiff Xie Minshi and Zhang Ruichang.

After this preliminary judgment was rendered, neither party appealed, and the judgment of first instance took effect. After the judgment took effect, the defendants Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company applied to the examination and approval authority for the equity change. The examination and approval authority also, in accordance with the application, changed the investors of Jingang Company to Zhang Ruichang and the non-party entity Lixin Company.

After the execution of the preliminary judgment, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court again held a public hearing to try the matter concerning the payment of the equity transfer price between the parties.

Plaintiff Xie Minshi's Allegations: The defendant Zhang Ruichang and the defendant Jingang Company have, in accordance with the effective judgment, performed the equity change registration procedures. For this reason, Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company should pay the plaintiff the agreed equity transfer price of USD 400,000. Given that at the time the "March 13 Resolutions" were made, Jingang Company was experiencing operational difficulties, it was then agreed that Jingang Company would pay the equity transfer price after selling the relevant property. Now nearly two years have passed since the agreement was signed, and the operations of Jingang Company have improved. Therefore, the plaintiff requests that Zhang Ruichang and Jingang Company make payment immediately.

Defendant Zhang Ruichang's Defense: The basis of the "March 13 Resolutions" was the offsetting of the equity transfer price against the proceeds from the sale of the property. Since the actual sale of the relevant property was handled by the plaintiff Xie Minshi himself, and the property was not sold, the fault lies with Xie Minshi. Therefore, I do not agree to immediately pay Xie Minshi in cash. Furthermore, Xie Minshi's withdrawal of equity has placed significant pressure on the operations of Jingang Company, and Xie Minshi should share the losses caused to Jingang Company as a result.

Defendant Jingang Company's Defense: The plaintiff Xie Minshi's withdrawal of equity has indeed caused losses to the operations of this Company. It agrees with the opinion of the defendant Zhang Ruichang.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court ascertained through trial:

"3·13 Resolution" is divided into Parts A and B. Part A resolved: that Defendant Jingang Company and all directors agreed to transfer the property at Room 404, Building 7, Lane 65, Jinshajiang Road, Shanghai (including all interior decoration) to Plaintiff Xie Minshi at a price of RMB 421,145; the Company or its board members shall cooperate with Xie Minshi in handling the property transfer procedures and shall submit the relevant documents to Xie Minshi within two days of signing the resolution; the board agreed to sell the ground-floor shop at No. 69, Jinshajiang Road, Shanghai at a total price of RMB 2,706,545 with a 95% down payment, and RMB 1,500,000 of the down payment from the sale shall be paid to Xie Minshi, with the balance paid to Zhang Ruichang; the valuation and sale proceeds of the properties shall serve as part of the equity transfer payment to be made by Zhang Ruichang, and the payment of the remaining equity transfer price shall be adjusted by Part B. Part B resolved: that Xie Minshi's 20% equity interest in Jingang Company is valued at USD 400,000 or RMB 3,311,600. Pursuant to Part A, the equity transfer payment actually made by Zhang Ruichang through property valuation and sale proceeds was RMB 1,921,145. Of this amount, within two days of receiving the RMB 1,500,000 from the shop sale, Xie Minshi shall make a loan of RMB 270,000 to Jingang Company as financial assistance, with a term of two months, and this RMB 270,000 shall be repaid by Jingang Company or Zhang Ruichang in two monthly installments; Zhang Ruichang shall transfer his entire equity interest in KINGSTON FOUNDRY & MACHINING INC., USA, valued at USD 26,000 (equivalent to RMB 215,245), to Xie Minshi, and Zhang Ruichang shall deliver all shares of said company to Xie Minshi, with this amount also offsetting the equity transfer price; the area loss of the ground-floor shop at No. 69, Jinshajiang Road resulting from this sale, amounting to RMB 114,239, shall be borne by Xie Minshi and deducted from the equity transfer price; meanwhile, the appreciation profit from the sale of the shop, amounting to RMB 195,295, shall be disposed of by Jingang Company or Zhang Ruichang; after offsetting these amounts, the remaining balance of the equity transfer price that Zhang Ruichang must pay to Xie Minshi is RMB 1,060,971, payable in twelve monthly installments commencing from the third month after the execution of this agreement.

The above facts are not disputed by either party and shall be confirmed.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held that:

Article 84 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC* provides: "A debt represents a specific relationship of rights and obligations established between parties according to the terms of a contract or the provisions of law. The party entitled to rights is the creditor, and the party obligated to perform is the debtor." "The creditor has the right to demand that the debtor perform the obligation according to the terms of the contract or the provisions of law." The "3·13 Resolution" is an agreement reached at the board meeting of Defendant Jingang Company regarding the equity transfer between Plaintiff Xie Minshi and Defendant Zhang Ruichang, and all parties shall abide by it.

Pursuant to the "3·13 Resolution," Defendant Jingang Company agreed to use its properties to offset the equity transfer payment owed by Defendant Zhang Ruichang to Plaintiff Xie Minshi, which constitutes an assumption of debt. Jingang Company bears limited liability in this case, meaning it is liable for debt settlement only to the extent of the properties used for debt offset.

With respect to the property valued for debt offset, Defendant Jingang Company shall transfer the property to Plaintiff Xie Minshi at the agreed price to satisfy the debt. With respect to the property that was to be sold at an agreed price and then used for debt offset, since that property has not yet been sold and there is currently no buyer who can exactly purchase it at the price set in the "3·13 Resolution," the method of disposal agreed for that property in the resolution has lost its basis for performance. Without jeopardizing the interests of Jingang Company's other creditors, the obligation with respect to this property may be performed by the parties revaluing the property or by Jingang Company selling it and using the proceeds to repay the debt. If the proceeds from Jingang Company's sale of the property for debt repayment fall short of the originally agreed repayment amount, the shortfall shall be supplemented by Defendant Zhang Ruichang, and Jingang Company shall have no further liability.

A debtor shall unconditionally repay its debt to the creditor. Regarding the "3·13 Resolution," in which the parties negotiated how to pay the equity transfer price owed by Defendant Zhang Ruichang to Plaintiff Xie Minshi, the provision requiring Xie Minshi to make a loan to Jingang Company as financial assistance was evidently a term pushed by the debtor using the debt repayment as a condition, contrary to the true intention of the creditor. This provision does not comply with the legal requirement that a contract reflect the true intention of the parties and is therefore void.

With respect to the "3·13 Resolution" provision that Defendant Zhang Ruichang's entire equity interest in KINGSTON FOUNDRY & MACHINING INC., USA would be offset and transferred to Plaintiff Xie Minshi, Zhang Ruichang did not adduce evidence to prove that he had delivered the relevant shares to Xie Minshi. Moreover, this matter involves the share transfer procedures of a foreign company. Therefore, the court shall not address this issue in this case, and it shall be resolved separately by Xie Minshi and Zhang Ruichang.

In conclusion, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on March 31, 2002:

1. Defendant Zhang Ruichang shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay Plaintiff Xie Minshi the equity transfer price of USD 400,000 or RMB 3,311,600.

2. With respect to the debt of Defendant Zhang Ruichang under the preceding paragraph, Defendant Jingang Company shall bear joint and several liability limited to the property agreed upon by the parties (Room 404, Building 7, Lane 65, Jinshajiang Road, Shanghai; and the ground-floor shop at No. 69, Jinshajiang Road, Shanghai). The specific methods of performance are as follows:

   (i) Defendant Jingang Company shall transfer the property at Room 404, Building 7, Lane 65, Jinshajiang Road, Shanghai to Plaintiff Xie Minshi, with the property valued at RMB 421,145.

   (ii) Defendant Jingang Company shall sell the ground-floor shop at No. 69, Jinshajiang Road, Shanghai and apply the proceeds to satisfy the debt of Defendant Zhang Ruichang under Paragraph 1 of this judgment.

3. The remaining claims of Plaintiff Xie Minshi are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee: RMB 26,568; property preservation application fee: RMB 19,520; total: RMB 46,080, to be borne by Defendant Zhang Ruichang.

After the judgment was rendered, neither party appealed, and the judgment of first instance became legally effective.
